hints: Look carefully at each label and name it first. Which numbers are atria, and which numbers are large arteries leaving the ventricles?
Remember the golden rule: blood always goes atrium to ventricle to artery, with the left side sending blood to the body (via 1) and the right side sending blood to the lungs (via 4).
walkthrough:
**Identify the four labelled structures**

First, orient yourself. The apex points down, so the left side of the picture is the right side of the heart.

Label 2 is the left atrium, label 3 is the right atrium, label 1 is the aorta (systemic artery to the body), label 4 is the pulmonary artery (to the lungs).

**Follow the left side of the heart first**

Oxygenated blood in the left atrium (2) flows down into the left ventricle, then is pumped out through the aorta (1) to the body.

So we must start with: $2 \rightarrow 1$

**Follow the right side of the heart next**

After circulating the body, deoxygenated blood returns to the right atrium (3), flows down into the right ventricle, then is pumped out through the pulmonary artery (4) to the lungs.

So the second half must be: $3 \rightarrow 4$

**Join the two halves together**

Blood goes through the left heart, round the body, then through the right heart to the lungs. That gives the full sequence $2 \rightarrow 1 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow 4$, which is option B.

options.A: Incorrect, blood cannot go from aorta (1) to left atrium (2) or from right atrium (3) to pulmonary artery (4) without passing through a ventricle first.
options.B: Correct, left atrium (2) to aorta (1) represents systemic flow, then right atrium (3) to pulmonary artery (4) represents pulmonary flow.
options.C: Incorrect, starting at 3 and going to 4 skips the right ventricle, and blood cannot go from aorta (1) back into left atrium (2).
options.D: Incorrect, this is backwards. Arteries (4 and 1) carry blood away from ventricles, they never empty directly into atria (3 and 2).
